FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.IndependentStudentQuestion: Why does a quadratic polynomial need a branch restriction for a functional inverse, whereas y=x³ does not?
FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.TeacherExpectedMath: x² gives the same output for ±x, so is not injective over all real inputs. x³ is strictly increasing, so its inverse cube root is a function.
FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.OriginalSourceMathReviewed: An inverse is a function only if its original mapping is one-to-one on the stated domain.

FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.IndependentStudentQuestion: Explain which branch of y=x²+6 would yield inverse y=√(x−6).
FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.TeacherExpectedMath: Restrict original x≥0; then the inverse outputs are nonnegative and its domain is x≥6.
FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.OriginalSourceMathReviewed: A quadratic has two branches; choose one to define a function inverse.

FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.IndependentStudentQuestion: What domain restriction does the inverse of f(x)=√(x+2) need?
FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.TeacherExpectedMath: The inverse f⁻¹(x)=x²−2 has domain x≥0, because original square-root outputs are nonnegative.
FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.OriginalSourceMathReviewed: The inverse domain equals the original range.

FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.IndependentStudentQuestion: Write the general form of the inverse of y=(x−h)²+k on original x≥h.
FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.OriginalSourceMathReviewed: Restricted quadratic inverses use the principal positive square-root branch.
Original source #5: f=(x−4)², x≥4; inverse 4+√x, x≥0.

FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.IndependentStudentQuestion: Invert f(x)=5−√(x+1); give inverse input domain.
Sketch f(x)=x²+5 on x≥0, and sketch its inverse reflection across y=x.
FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.TeacherExpectedMath: Inverse √(x−5) on input x≥5. Corresponding points (0,5)↔(5,0), (2,9)↔(9,2).
FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.OriginalSourceMathReviewed: Source #32: x²+2, x≥0 has inverse √(x−2); points swap over y=x.

FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.IndependentStudentQuestion: Sketch f(x)=9−x² on x≥0 with its inverse.
FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.OriginalSourceMathReviewed: Source #33: 4−x² on x≥0 inverse √(4−x), input x≤4.

FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.IndependentStudentQuestion: Sketch f(x)=(x+4)² on x≥−4 and its inverse.
Sketch f(x)=(x−5)² on x≥5 and its inverse.
Sketch f(x)=x²+2x on x≥−1 and its inverse.
Sketch f(x)=x²−4x+3 on x≥2 and its inverse.

FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.TeacherExpectedMath: Self-inverse 3/x; both graphs symmetric about y=x, points (1,3)↔(3,1).
FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.OriginalSourceMathReviewed: Source #40: 2/x is self-inverse on nonzero reals.

FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.IndependentStudentQuestion: Sketch f(x)=4/x² on x>0 and its inverse.
FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.TeacherExpectedMath: Inverse 2/√x for x>0; points (1,4)↔(4,1). Domain original must exclude x=0.
FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.OriginalSourceMathReviewed: Source #41: 1/x² restricted x>0 inverse 1/√x for x>0.

FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.IndependentStudentQuestion: Find domain of √(((x−2)(x+1))/x) by sign chart.

FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.OriginalSourceMathReviewed: Source #47: f=x³−x−2, original inputs1,2,3 give inverse points (−2,1),(4,2),(22,3).

FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.IndependentStudentQuestion: For f(x)=x³+x+2, give inverse points with y=0,1,2.
For f(x)=x³+2x−3, give inverse points with y=0,1,2.
For f(x)=x³+4x−2, give inverse points with y=−1,0,1.
For the inverse relation of f(x)=x⁴+4x+2, list three swapped points for original x=−1,0,1 and explain why a domain restriction may be necessary.
FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.TeacherExpectedMath: Inverse relation points (−1,−1),(2,0),(7,1). f is not globally one-to-one, so these swapped points do not establish a global inverse function.
FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.OriginalSourceMathReviewed: Source #51: x⁴+5x+1 gives inverse-relation points (−3,−1),(1,0),(7,1); global inverse function requires suitable domain restriction.

FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.IndependentStudentQuestion: For b>0 and x≥−b, invert f(x)=x²+2bx.
FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.OriginalSourceMathReviewed: Source #53: x²+bx not one-to-one over all reals. On x≥−b/2 inverse (−b+√(b²+4x))/2; original missing branch restriction.

FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.IndependentStudentQuestion: For a,b>0 and original x≥0, invert f(x)=√(2ax²+b).
FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.OriginalSourceMathReviewed: Source #54: √(ax²+b) not globally one-to-one. With x≥0, inverse √((x²−b)/a), x≥√b.

FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.TeacherExpectedMath: f⁻¹(x)=(2b−cx)/(x−a), x≠a; requires nonconstant original mapping (2b≠ac).
FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.OriginalSourceMathReviewed: Source #56: (ax+b)/(x+c) inverse (b−cx)/(x−a) provided b≠ac; if b=ac function is constant a and has no inverse function.

FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.IndependentStudentQuestion: An object falls from 180 m with h(t)=180−5t² for t≥0. Express t(h) and time at height80 m.
FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.TeacherExpectedMath: t(h)=√((180−h)/5) seconds; at h=80, t=√20≈4.472 seconds.

FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.OriginalSourceMathReviewed: Source #60 incorrectly says r as function V though the expression is surface area A. Correct r(A)=√(A/(4π)); at A1000 in² r=√(250/π) in.

FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.IndependentStudentQuestion: For a closed cylinder height3 ft, surface area A=2πr²+6πr. Find inverse r(A) and radius at A=20π ft².

FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.IndependentStudentQuestion: A cone has height12 inches and volume16π cubic inches. Find radius with consistent units.
FirstPartyIndependentStudentMathQuestion.OriginalSourceMathReviewed: Source #65 mixes 12-foot height with 50 cubic inches volume; must convert h to144 inches before using in³. Source prompt also ambiguously says r in terms h, although h is fixed.
